expectations.text: [0.1] A notification port interface is declared, and since nothing outside server/ names it, it lives beside its adapter (adapters/notifier/) rather than widening the client-mirrored vendor/shared surface
expectations.evidence: server-only Notifier port pushed into the client-mirrored vendor/shared/adapters.ts
expectations.rule: Where does the port interface go? — server-local ports live beside their adapter

expectations.text: [0.2] The concrete implementation (the HTTP POST to the webhook) lives in a file under server/src/adapters/
expectations.rule: Layer map — infrastructure

expectations.text: [0.3] No service.ts performs the HTTP call itself (no fetch/axios/undici/WebClient inside modules/*/service.ts)
expectations.evidence: no service.ts performs the HTTP call
expectations.rule: Hard rule 3 — no direct SDK/HTTP construction in a service

expectations.text: [0.4] The adapter is wired in server/src/platform/container.ts
expectations.rule: Hard rule 6 — compose only at the root

expectations.text: [0.5] The service receives the notifier as an injected dependency and does not construct the adapter itself (no `new <Adapter>(` in service.ts)
expectations.evidence: service receives the notifier as an injected dependency
expectations.rule: Hard rule 6 — a service receives its dependencies

expectations.text: [0.6] The webhook URL comes from config/secrets, not a hardcoded literal URL in the service or adapter
expectations.rule: Config/secrets convention

expectations.text: [1.1] routes.ts contains no Drizzle/SQL query (no drizzle-orm import, no db.select/count/sql usage)
expectations.rule: Hard rule 4 — routes are thin

expectations.text: [1.2] The aggregation query lives in repository.ts
expectations.rule: Layer map — infrastructure

expectations.text: [1.3] A service.ts orchestrates: the route calls the service, the service calls the repository
expectations.rule: Layer map — application

expectations.text: [1.4] The response shape is defined as a Zod schema under server/src/vendor/shared/contracts/
expectations.rule: Decision rule — contracts live in vendor/shared/contracts

expectations.text: [1.5] Row -> DTO conversion happens in helpers.ts and no raw Drizzle row is handed to HTTP
expectations.rule: Hard rule 5 — map at the boundary

expectations.text: [1.6] The query is workspace-scoped (filters on workspace_id / uses the request's workspace context)
expectations.rule: Tenancy (server/CLAUDE.md)

expectations.text: [2.1] No file under reviewer-core/ imports Octokit or any GitHub/HTTP SDK
expectations.rule: Hard rule 2 — keep the core pure

expectations.text: [2.2] No file under reviewer-core/ performs network or filesystem I/O (no fetch/axios/node:fs/node:https)
expectations.rule: Hard rule 2 — reviewer-core performs zero I/O

expectations.text: [2.3] The GitHub read happens on the server side through the existing GitHubClient port resolved from the Container (no ad-hoc Octokit construction)
expectations.evidence: GitHub reached via the GitHubClient port in server/src/modules/reviews/run-executor.ts
expectations.rule: Hard rule 3 — external systems reached via ports

expectations.text: [2.4] The open-PR/conflict data enters reviewer-core as plain injected input (a field on the review input or an injected port), not fetched by reviewer-core itself
expectations.evidence: reviewer-core/src/conflicts.ts takes the open-PR data as plain input
expectations.rule: Hard rule 1 — dependencies point inward

expectations.text: [2.5] No GitHub/HTTP dependency is added to reviewer-core/package.json
expectations.rule: Hard rule 2 — the core stays dependency-free
